Order reduction in SDC with time-dependent Dirichlet boundary conditions

This report reproduces the classic order-reduction phenomenon for Spectral Deferred Corrections (SDC) applied to the forced 1D heat equation discretized in space with FEniCS finite elements. It compares two manufactured solutions of ut = ν uxx + f(x,t) on Ω = [0,1]:

  • Sine case (fenics_heat_mass): u(x,t) = sin(πx) cos(t) + c. Since sin(π·0) = sin(π·1) = 0, the Dirichlet boundary values are constant in time (equal to c).
  • Cosine case (fenics_heat_mass_timebc): u(x,t) = cos(πx) cos(t) + c. Now cos(π·0)=1, cos(π·1)=−1, so the boundary values ±cos(t)+c change in time. The BC is imposed directly on the right-hand side inside solve_system via bc.apply(b.values.vector()), which breaks the collocation fixed point and reduces the observed convergence order.
  • Cosine + internal lifting (fenics_heat_mass_timebc_lift_physical): integrates the homogeneous lifted variable internally, reconstructs the physical solution, and keeps the exact cosine solution unchanged.
Numerical setup
  • Tend = 1.0
  • dts = [0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125]
  • quad_type = RADAU-RIGHT
  • c_nvars = 256
  • nu = 0.1
  • c = 1.0
  • order = 4
  • refinements = 1
  • sweeper: imex_1st_order_mass (IMEX, mass-matrix formulation)
  • iterated to residual tolerance so the SDC solution reaches the collocation solution
  • error = relative error |uh − uexact| / |uexact| at Tend

The reference dashed line in each convergence plot has the full theoretical slope 2M−1. The local order plot shows the slope computed between successive time-step pairs, which reveals the asymptotic behaviour before the (spatial) error floor is reached.

M = 2 collocation nodes  (RADAU-RIGHT, expected order 2M−1 = 3)

At the largest time steps (cleanest asymptotic regime, before the spatial error floor is reached), the sine case attains local order 2.96 — essentially the full SDC order 3 — while the cosine (time-dependent BC) case attains only 2.75, a clear order reduction of about 0.2. With internal boundary lifting, the cosine case recovers 2.78 on the same interval.

At the largest time steps (cleanest asymptotic regime, before the spatial error floor is reached), the sine case attains local order 4.98 — essentially the full SDC order 5 — while the cosine (time-dependent BC) case attains only 4.47, a clear order reduction of about 0.5. With internal boundary lifting, the cosine case recovers 4.87 on the same interval.

Nonlinear Extension: Manufactured Reaction-Diffusion

The same three-way experiment was repeated for ut = νuxx + λu(1-u) + f(x,t) using a manufactured solution. The nonlinear reaction is evaluated at the reconstructed physical state u=v+E in the lifted formulation, and every implicit node solve uses Newton iteration.

For M=3, the nonlinear sine case reaches order 5, direct time-dependent BC imposition reduces the cosine case to approximately order 4.1, and lifting restores approximately order 4.9.

Increasing Difficulty: Nonlinear Diffusion

The diffusion operator is now the nonlinear flux ∂x((1+γu2)ux). The implicit SDC node equations are solved with Newton iteration. In the lifted formulation the nonlinear flux is evaluated at the physical state u=v+E, including the lift gradient in the face flux.

The sine case approaches the full fifth order. Direct time-dependent cosine BC imposition settles near order 4.1, while lifting trends toward order 5; the final local lifted orders are 4.51 and 4.71. This is a stronger test because the lift enters the nonlinear diffusion operator itself.

Summary

The linear sine case (constant-in-time boundary data) converges with the full SDC order 2M−1. The cosine case, whose Dirichlet data varies in time and is imposed naively on the right-hand side, exhibits a clear order reduction: for M=3 the order drops from the expected 5 to roughly 4.4. The internally lifted cosine case recovers the full order while retaining the same physical exact solution. The effect is milder for M=2 and largely a pre-asymptotic phenomenon there. Below the spatial error floor (≈ 10−10 for these settings) the temporal order can no longer be measured, which is why the smallest-Δt local orders in the M=3 plots collapse.

The nonlinear reaction-diffusion extension shows the same mechanism: order 5 for time-independent boundary data, approximately order 4.1 after naive time-dependent BC imposition, and approximately order 4.9 after boundary lifting.

The nonlinear-diffusion extension places the lift inside the nonlinear flux: the direct cosine case remains around order 4.1, while the lifted case trends upward toward the full fifth order.
